scores.rationale: Strongest arithmetic and validation story: fixed Pantone dictionary, prose-vs-POM number cross-check, Arabic-script/Latin-digit validators, ES 7266 label presence check, and a repair loop with a strict convergence guard. Marker efficiency 0.80 is optimistic for circular hat pieces (existing code uses 0.62, which a cutting room would believe). Factory readiness is solid (op sheet, Tex, AQL, acknowledgement block) but the document is ordered for evaluators, not for a sample room, and there is no Arabic-first sheet. Demo is a progress timeline with a spinner-ish feel; no progressive reveal or pre-rendered exports. Build risk: its own description undercounts the existing scaffold (2.7k vs 4.3k lines actually present), its schema outline (meta.brand etc.) diverges from the existing header/product shape, the zoom tool combined with output_config.format is an untested API interaction it admits may 400, and 9 days is the longest estimate.

scores.design: Design 2: Masdr Tech Pack — AI Tech Pack Generator (demo-impact-first)
scores.rationale: Same code-derived grading, provenance and validators as the others, matches the existing 4.3k-line scaffold exactly (header/product schema, edit.ts regrade, pdf/xlsx export, SSE, SQLite all present), and 7 days is the most credible estimate. Parallel draft split is a real latency win but introduces a cross-reference risk between BOM refs (3a) and operations (3b) that is only mitigated by convention. Progressive section reveal, 'What the AI saw' card, pre-rendered instant exports, live regrade of M and the factories-handoff modal give the best 3-minute demo. From the factory chair it is good (14-step op sheet, Tex/needle, ES 7266 label, AQL, same-hat note) but lacks an acknowledgement loop and an Arabic-first cutter/sewer sheet. Arm64 build-on-box is fine but adds deploy time and one more thing that can break; sample-review loop absent.

This is the pack an Egyptian merchandiser and sample room would actually use: sections in cutting-room order, Arabic-first sample-room sheet (cut sheet + op sheet + POM chart), factory acknowledgement form (sample size, units, tolerances, lot shrinkage, thread availability, lead time), sample-review rounds tied to POM codes with measured-vs-spec deltas, immutable versions, share link/QR, unresolved repair issues surfaced as questions for the factory. Correctness matches Design 2 with the useful cheap Sonnet detail-zoom on sharp crops. Build risk is the weakest: t3.small (2 GiB) with Chromium and 3 concurrent jobs will OOM, it proposes eu-central-1 against the client-confirmed eu-west-1, and adds three new human/LLM stages plus tokenised share pages on top of an 8-day estimate. Demo impact is fine but the extra loops are hard to show in 3 minutes without a second actor.

scores.rationale: Strongest correctness story: prose-vs-POM number cross-check, Arabic-script/Latin-digit validators, fixed Pantone dictionary, range clamps logged as assumptions, and a repair loop with a strict convergence guard. But it underestimates what already exists (cites ~2.7k lines; the scaffold is 4.3k with pipeline, edit, exports, SSE already in place), adds a zoom tool-use loop inside the vision call whose interaction with output_config.format is an acknowledged unknown, has no progressive section reveal (70 s of stage dots), renders exports on click (6-10 s Chromium hit mid-demo), and self-estimates 9 days for a 7-day window. x86_64 t3.medium build parity is the right call.

Same code-derived geometry, validators, provenance and bounded repair as the others, and its description of the existing scaffold is the only accurate one (single draft stage, critique, repair, applyPackEdit, PDF/XLSX/JSON, SSE all verified present), so the remaining-work list is credible at 7 days. Progressive partial-JSON section reveal, 'What the AI saw' card, pre-rendered exports, live regrade-on-edit and a labelled 'Replay cached run' fallback are exactly what a 3-minute evaluator demo needs. Deductions: the parallel DraftCore/DraftProduction split means two schemas, two prompts and a repair path over both, with cross-reference consistency held only by convention; it lacks Design 1's prose-vs-POM and Arabic validators; and building on an arm64 t4g box (pnpm install + build + Chromium deps on Graviton) is the riskiest infra choice of the three when the dev machine is x86_64 WSL2.

The most complete factory artefact: acknowledgement loop, sample-review rounds tied to POM codes with measured-vs-spec deltas, Arabic-first sample-room sheet, immutable versions, glossary check, and a cheap conditional Sonnet detail-zoom on sharp crops (simpler and safer than Design 1's tool loop). But it is 12 stages, three new SQLite tables, share tokens, QR codes, two PDF modes, an 11-sheet workbook and an extra LLM stage on top of the existing scaffold, none of which exists today; for one engineer in one week that is over-scoped and the 3-minute demo cannot show the loop end to end. t3.small (2 GiB) with Node + Chromium is a genuine OOM hazard it admits itself. Lower per-pack differentiation on the progress screen (no section reveal).
